notice: Python and libraries on this page: the page's own programs (the playground) run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with pyttsx3 2.99, openai-whisper 20250625, yt-dlp 2026.8.19, torch 2.14.1 (CPU), NumPy 2.5.4, eSpeak NG 1.51 and ffmpeg 6.1.1. A browser has no eSpeak NG or ffmpeg, cannot start programs and does not have pyttsx3, Whisper or yt-dlp, so none of the 74 examples of the chapter runs here: every one is shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run, each with its reason. Stand-ins: there is no sound card, so nothing was heard and the speech went to WAV files, a local stand-in for a loudspeaker; archive.org public-domain audio stands in for YouTube, which the research never downloaded from. The five pictures under five concepts were drawn by the deck's programs from audio that eSpeak NG spoke; they were not made on this page. Findings kept, not successes: transcription with Whisper medium and turbo was killed at about 6 GB of memory, and large-v3 (3,087,371,615 bytes) does not load. The deck, whose text is the Lecture tab, marks slides 5, 8, 12, 19 and 23 NOT EXECUTED (slide 5: SAPI5 on Windows, NSSpeechSynthesizer and AVSpeech on macOS, a microphone, a GPU and the cloud services of OpenAI, Google and Microsoft, only the eSpeak NG driver on Linux ran; slide 8: SAPI5 on Windows and NSSpeechSynthesizer on macOS; slide 12: transcription with medium and turbo, with large-v3 and on a GPU; slide 19: a download from YouTube, whose Terms of Service do not allow it; slide 23: SAPI5, NSSpeechSynthesizer and AVSpeech, a microphone, a GPU, the OpenAI, Google Cloud and Azure speech services, faster-whisper, whisper.cpp, SpeechRecognition, gTTS and Vosk, Whisper medium, turbo and large-v3, and any download from YouTube), calls slides 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15, 18, 19, 20 and 23 Recorded (results of 14 October 2026 that it does not run again).
